title: Simple Habits for a Clog-Free Kitchen Drain
description: Kitchen drains handle grease, food scraps, and soap daily, making them prone to slow draining and stubborn clogs. To keep your lines clear, avoid pouring cooking oils or fats down the sink—grease cools and solidifies inside your pipes. Always scrape plates into the trash before washing, and use a mesh drain strainer to catch stray debris. Once a week, flush the drain with hot water to wash away soft buildup. Regularly inspect the under-sink P-trap for minor leaks or signs of blockage. If water backs up continuously, consult a licensed plumber to clear deeper mainline obstructions safely.
